response: Yes, T-cell deficiency can affect spatial learning ability following toluene exposure. Research suggests that immune system dysfunction, including T-cell deficiency, can exacerbate the neurotoxic effects of toluene, a solvent known to impair cognitive function, particularly spatial learning and memory. The absence or impairment of T-cells may disrupt the normal immune response and increase the vulnerability of the brain to toluene-induced damage, leading to impaired spatial learning ability.
